hypothesis: On one newly generated synthetic sequence, fixed imbalance decisions achieve higher held-out net ticks-times-lots than the fixed seeded random control after spread and fees. This is a plumbing comparison, not an alpha hypothesis about real markets.
input: research.generate, replayed by the exact locally built C++ replay_events executable
holdout: Existing research.lab chronological last 40% of BBO observations; training labels are purged by delay+horizon. No results inspected before this plan.
primary_metric: imbalance execution.net_pnl_ticks_lots minus random execution.net_pnl_ticks_lots on the same held-out observations
ablation: Existing cost sensitivity panel, with fixed decisions/parameters; report zero-cost and higher-cost results where supplied. No selection based on ablation.
parameter_search: none; exactly one seed, fixed config, no retries to improve measured results
stress: Run the checked-in terminal-depth fixture and plan unchanged; retain fees, observation latency, spread and depth assumptions and adverse open-inventory result. This fixture is separate from the held-out comparison.
benchmark: Existing bench_rdtsc, 2M deterministic operations and 100K warmup, three repeats on one build/host. Separate serialized engine timing, streaming engine rate, and SPSC pipeline. Retain affinity warnings, variance, compiler flags, binary/source fingerprints. No cross-version speed claim.
limitations: Synthetic input only; no real market evidence or live trading
Labels overlap within partitions; no independent-sample significance estimate
No queue position, impact, financing, or venue realism
Latency is measured in observations, not milliseconds
Benchmark host load is not controlled
